image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a grey whale surfacing in teal ocean water. The whale's head and upper back are visible, showing characteristic mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. A portion of a blue and yellow boat is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle is from the side/top-front; the blowholes are not clearly visible due to the viewing angle and water reflection, making this specific feature untestable.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white/lighter patches consistent with barnacle encrustation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the back behind the head shows a smooth ridge without a vertical dorsal fin, consistent with the 'dorsal knuckle' anatomy of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior section of the whale is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified from this cropped view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; the visible body skin matches the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and submerged; baleen plates are internal and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are submerged and not visible in this surface-level shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture of the skin appears rough and uneven, consistent with callosities and barnacle bases.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification based on skin pattern and head shape, distinguishing it from other cetaceans.
To detect subtle AI artifacts in the complex texture of the skin and the interaction with the water (splashes/reflections).
To ensure the boundary between the whale and the water is physically consistent and not suffering from 'melting' or edge bleeding.
To verify the spatial relationship and depth consistency between the foreground boat and the whale.

focus_areas: Anatomical correctness of visible head/back features
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the water line around the whale. AI often struggles with the complex refraction and splash patterns where a large object breaks the water surface. Verify if the white patches look like attached biological entities (barnacles) or just painted-on noise.
